Then the command went forth that he should be killed.
And the Mongols hung him up by his hands and his feet above,
and three times they dashed him to the ground,
trampling him with their boots until he expired.
Then they cut off his head on Tuesday, the 1[6th]
of Sha'ban, in the year 683
683 of the Arabs,
that is, the 17th
of the First Tishrin [October],
the year 1596 [AG].
And the whole kingdom of the house of Magog hung upon his finger,
for he was exceedingly crafty with natural intelligence,
and also accomplished in many sciences and learning.
His brother, however, 'Ala al-Din,
who was the governor of Baghdad,
who had died a natural death in Mugan a little less than two years earlier,
and was brought to the city of Tabriz and buried there,
this man too was exceedingly skilled in sciences and competent in poetry.
And he composed a wonderful book of history in Persian on the kingdom of the Seljuks, the Khwarazmians, the Ismailis, and the Mongols;
and from his book we have taken that which we have cited in this book of ours concerning these events.
And in that same year 683
683 of the Arabs,
there died also Sultan Ghiyath al-Din, son of Rukn al-Din, the ruler of the country of the Romans [Rum].
For he had set out to come to the Ordu,
and to complain against Sultan Mas'ud, his cousin.
And when he reached the city of Erzincan,
the grandees made him drink deadly poison and killed him,
because he conducted himself very recklessly and with confused intelligence.
And in this winter, all seven wandering stars [planets] gathered in the zodiacal sign of Capricorn in Anabibazon [the Ascending Node];
and behold, the world trembled and shook thereby,
because the year was the conjunction of the two superior ones, Kronos [Saturn] and Zeus [Jupiter], in the sign of Aquarius;
for they make a synod [conjunction] in the summer.
And the ruler of Egypt, when he heard that the kingdom was firmly established for Arghun,
and that Ahmad had departed and his peace along with him,
brought out Sheikh 'Abd al-Rahman from the prison of the fortress,
and made him dwell in one of ... [Footnote text: whatever happens in the world does not happen from the conjunction of the luminaries, nor does it happen from their assembly,
but by the will of the Lord,
without whom not even one sparrow falls to the ground.
